title: Shout it back and count the words
description: Write a script that asks the user for a sentence, prints it back entirely in uppercase, and then prints how many words it contains.
examples:
Enter a sentence: hello world foo
HELLO WORLD FOO
Word count: 3
hints: Read the sentence with input(), then think about which string method changes every letter to uppercase.
str.upper() returns an uppercase copy of a string, and str.split() breaks a string into a list of words on whitespace by default.
Print sentence.upper() on its own line, then print an f-string that reads exactly 'Word count: ' followed by len(sentence.split()).
expected_behavior: Reads a sentence, prints it fully uppercased, then prints the number of whitespace-separated words it contains.

hidden_tests.expected_stdout:
Enter a sentence: HELLO WORLD FOO
Word count: 3
hidden_tests.label: three words

hidden_tests.expected_stdout:
Enter a sentence: PYTHON IS FUN
Word count: 3
hidden_tests.label: three words, different sentence

hidden_tests.expected_stdout:
Enter a sentence: HI
Word count: 1
hidden_tests.label: single word

explanation: str.upper() returns a new string with every letter capitalized, and str.split() splits on any run of whitespace, producing a list whose length is the word count.
